description.narrative: EU-kommissionen har beslutat att avsätta totalt 40 miljoner euro från EU:s Sk "Emergency Trust Fund" för att stödja genomförandet av IGAD:s freds- och säkerhetsstrategi under perioden 2018-2022, varav 5 miljoner Euro kommer gå till lönekostnader och 35 miljoner euro tilldelas 'IGAD Promoting Peace and Stability in the Horn of Africa Region', IPPSHAR-programmet. Programmets riktning är helt i linje med den svenska strategin och dess fokus på förstärkt kapacitet bland regionala aktörer för fred och försoning, ökat kvinnligt deltagande i fredsprocesser och bekämpning av våldsbejakande extremism. Sverige kommer att tilldela 10,5 miljoner kronor för genomförandet av programmet, pengarna kommer att ställas till förfogande för användandet av Österrikes Biståndsorgan, ADA, som är utsedd som partner ansvarig för genomförande av det delegerade EU-avtalet och Sidas bidrag. ADA bidrar med ytterligare 1 million Euro till programmet och Nederländerna bidrar med ca 600.000 euro. Insatsens totala summa är därför 42,6 miljoner euro.

The EU Commission has decided to allocate a total of EURO 40 million from the EU Trust Fund to support the implementation of IGAD's Peace and Security Strategy during the period 2018-2022, of which 5 million euro will go to salary costs and 35 million will go to the 'IGAD Promoting Peace and Stability in the Horn of Africa Region, IPPSHAR, programme.The direction of the programme is fully in line with the Swedish strategy, and its focus on strengthened capacities among regional actors for peace and reconciliation, increased women's participation in processes for peace, and combating of violent extremism. Sweden will allocate 10,5 MSEK for the implementation of the programme, the funds will be made available for the use of the Austrian Development Agency (ADA) who has been appointed as the managing agent of the delegated EU-agreement as well as Sida's contribution. ADA is contributing an additional 1 million euro to the IPPSHAR programme and the Netherlands is contributing with 676,579 euro. The total contribution amount is therefore 42.6 million euro.

The General objective is "to contribute to achieving sustainable peace, security and stability for the attainment of economic integration and development in the IGAD region (Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda)." The Four specific objectives are:
1. To enhance the IGAD Conflict Early Warning and Response Mechanism (CEWARN) systems, so that there is an improvement in the quantity and quality of the information collected, in data analysis, and early response action 2. To enable IGAD and national governments in the region to predict, prevent, and address transnational security threats 3. To enhance the capacity of IGAD and national governments of the region on preventive diplomacy, mediation and civilian peace building 4. To enhance the implementation effectiveness of IGAD's Peace and Security Division (PSD) and units

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Some notable achievements through the programme's four Specific Objective (SO), includes:
Under (SO): 1 CEWARN implemented an extensive programme of work to strengthen early warning systems across the region. This included substantial work with national institutions through support for the CEWERUs and national research institutions (NRIs), which has facilitated increased collaboration and helped develop national platforms in MS to shape policy and develop appropriate national responses. The Rapid Response Fund (RRF) grants were targeted at areas across the region experiencing tension and conflict and were designed to channel funds through national structures to local implementing bodies on the ground. This has facilitated revised M&E Framework; defined three overall results areas; and increased collaboration between national institutions in the MS.
Under SO 2: the IGAD Security Sector Program (SSP) has focused on emerging security threats in the region and worked to build awareness and capacity among MS institutions on issues such as financing of terrorism, cybercrime and the use of technology to promote de-radicalisation and violent extremism. The IGAD SSP developed a strategic approach by networking key agencies in MS, building technical capacity across the region, and promoting the ratification of international norms and frameworks.
under SO 3 preventive diplomacy, mediation and civilian peace building: This was done through the support for the Ethiopian Ministry of Peace and the South Sudan Ministry of Peacebuilding and its efforts to develop national mediation strategies in MS. The project responded to developments in the transition processes in Sudan and in South Sudan through the allocation of contingency funding. This enabled IGAD to support the NCAC and the JRC in South Sudan and to play a role in the Trilateral Mechanism (TM) in Sudan in partnership with the African Union and the United Nations. The support provided to the IGAD Special Mission to Somalia enabled the Special Envoy to facilitate political dialogue in the lead up to the 2021/22 election and to engage in local dispute resolution processes. Despite the challenges and complexity in the region, the Mediation Support Unit (MSU) has made a valuable contribution to peace and stability, particularly by strengthening the capacity of civil society groups in several MS. The MSU also established and trained a roster of mediators and technical experts to support peacebuilding in the region. However, despite the needs in the region, this roster has not been utilised to its full potential so far.
SO 4: aimed to enhance the implementation effectiveness of the PSD and its units. The project supported the PSD units to carry out analysis and produce a range of knowledge products, as well as updating hardware and software in the PSD and in MS institutions. The management of the IPPSHAR project has built capacity in IGAD and strengthened the PSD in a number of key areas, particularly programme management, procurement, finance and compliance, M&E and communications. In addition, increased emphasis was put on more effective internal and external communication of the PSD and its units and institutions, including the development and upgrading of websites and apps and the establishment of hubs by the IFSI and the ICEPCVE.
